gap: No result ChatGPT got states which chargers can charge the XTAR 1.5 V AA 4150 mWh. XTAR's own FAQ names the VX4, MX4, L8, L4, BC8 and BC4, and rules out its own VC4, VC8, FC2 and VP4 Plus models. A NiMH-only charger such as the Tenergy TN480U, which Tenergy lists for NiMH only, cannot be used for it. The same FAQ says the cell is unsuitable for clocks, radios, flashlights of about 300 lm and up, and some camera flashes.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited and the top uncited result. Digital Camera World (cited) has only a general line that 1.5 V Li-ion cells suit 'voltage-critical devices'. It says nothing about chargers or devices to avoid. The Which? sample page (cited) gives only LADDA run time and charge time, with no charger or device compatibility. geekchamp (rank 2, not cited) gives a general warning, 'do not assume they charge 1.5V lithium rechargeable cells', and quotes a listing saying lithium cells work only with their own brand's charger. It names no XTAR charger models, no excluded chargers and no device exclusions. None of the three mentions smoke alarms. ChatGPT's answer said only that 1.5 V cells need 'their dedicated charger'.
decides: This confirms that the XTAR belongs on the page only as a niche pick, and it changes what that row should say. XTAR says to buy it with an XTAR L4, L8, VX4, MX4, BC4 or BC8 charger, and that the Tenergy TN480U we list will not charge it. XTAR's 'suitable' list is controllers, wireless mics, RC toys, trail cameras and multimeters, and its 'unsuitable' list includes clocks. Our row says 'Best for: smart locks, thermostats'. Thermostats are low-drain devices like clocks, so that line should be checked against XTAR's own guidance. XTAR's FAQ does not name thermostats; that comparison is mine. The NiMH picks (eneloop, eneloop pro, LADDA, Tenergy Premium Pro) can all share one NiMH charger such as the TN480U or IKEA STENKOL. First Alert says never to use rechargeable batteries in its smoke alarms, so the page should carve that use out for every pick.

findings.label: Chargers that can charge it (maker list)
findings.value: XTAR VX4, MX4, L8, L4, BC8, BC4
findings.source_title: FAQs about XTAR 4150mWh AA Li-ion Battery
findings.note: From XTAR's own FAQ. The cell needs a constant 5 V charge for its built-in management chip, so ordinary 3.6 V Li-ion and 18650 chargers cannot charge it.

findings.label: XTAR chargers that cannot charge it (maker exclusion)
findings.value: FC2, VC4, VC4SL, VC2SL, VC8, VC8S, VC8 PLUS, VP4L PLUS, VP4 PLUS
findings.source_title: FAQs about XTAR 4150mWh AA Li-ion Battery
findings.note: Several of XTAR's own popular chargers are excluded, so an XTAR-branded charger is not automatically compatible.

findings.label: Devices XTAR says it is unsuitable for
findings.value: Clocks (built-in circuit drains it quickly); radios (interference noise); flashlights of about 300 lm and up that draw about 2.5 A (protection cuts output above 2-2.5 A); some camera flashes (high instant current and heat)
findings.source_title: FAQs about XTAR 4150mWh AA Li-ion Battery
findings.note: Suitable uses on the same page: wireless microphones, VR and game controllers, RC toys, trail cameras, multimeters, sound mixers. XTAR also says self-discharge is higher than NiMH because of the built-in circuit. The 2,500 mAh rating is at a 0.5 A discharge, and the 1.5 V regulator loses about 8-10%.

findings.label: Chemistries it charges
findings.value: NiMH only, AA and AAA; 500 mA per AA bay, 250 mA per AAA bay; 5 V 2 A USB-C or micro-USB input; $23.99 charger only
findings.source_title: Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay NiMH Battery LCD Display Fast Charger, Micro USB/Type C Input (P/N 01480)
findings.note: The spec sheet says 'Compatible Chemistry: NiMH'. It does not mention lithium, which together with XTAR's own list means it cannot charge the XTAR 1.5 V cells. It should charge the NiMH picks (eneloop, eneloop pro, LADDA, Premium Pro), but the page names no other brands. Price read from the page on the date shown.

findings.label: Chargers IKEA names
findings.value: STENKOL or TJUGO; IKEA also says 'For rechargeable batteries, only use the intended charger'; STENKOL $8.99
findings.source_title: LADDA rechargeable battery, HR06 AA 1.2V, 2450mAh - IKEA US
findings.note: Price on the same page: $11.99 for 4. IKEA lists no devices to avoid and says LADDA is 'best in products with high energy consumption'. The page gives no cycle count and no self-discharge or retention figure.

findings.label: What it accepts (per IKEA product listings)
findings.value: NiMH AA and AAA only, minimum 1,000 mAh (AA) or 500 mAh (AAA); 4 independent channels; never charge non-rechargeable cells
findings.source_title: STENKOL / LADDA battery charger and 4 batteries - IKEA US
findings.note: This comes from a search summary of IKEA's STENKOL listings. I did not open this page myself, so verify it before publishing. It means STENKOL cannot charge 1.5 V lithium AAs either.

findings.label: Smoke alarms: maker exclusion of rechargeables
findings.value: First Alert: 'Never use rechargeable batteries because they may not always provide a consistent charge.'
findings.source_title: Smoke Alarms FAQ - First Alert Store
findings.note: This applies to every pick on the page, NiMH or 1.5 V lithium. First Alert recommends lithium smoke-detector batteries, meaning disposable ones. None of the rival pages mention smoke alarms.
